info.bio:
Jethro Tull es el nombre de una original banda de rock progresivo escocesa, que comenzó sus andaduras en 1968 y que, desde entonces, ha trabajado de forma ininterrumpida hasta el día de hoy, siendo, tras Rolling Stones (1962) y Le Orme (1966), entre otros, uno de los grupos de rock más antiguos todavía activo.

El nombre de la banda, extraño como suena, tiene un origen no menos particular. Su agente revisó libros de historia y llegó con el nombre de Jethro Tull

scenes.name: Rock progresivo
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Al emigrar a Gran Bretaña, el rock se convierte en mercancía de moda pero también se descontextualiza: lo que en EE UU era el diario de la juventud se vuelve en Gran Bretaña un ensayo. El progresivo no comenta la cultura juvenil sino que busca la innovación técnica: arranca con las óperas rock (S.F. Sorrow, Tommy) y los álbumes conceptuales, lo cimentan Traffic, Jeff Beck, Jethro Tull, Family y Genesis, y alcanza su cima con King Crimson (In The Court Of The Crimson King), Van Der Graaf Generator y Yes. Colosseum, la Third Ear Band (inventores de la world music), las variantes góticas (High Tide, Black Widow) y folk (Comus, Strawbs), Gentle Giant, Emerson Lake & Palmer y Roxy Music, que revoluciona el género y prepara la new wave y el synth-pop.

podcast.title: Anti-Streaming Stance
podcast.body: Jethro Tull refuses to have any of their discography on Spotify, and generally opposes any digital support, including digital downloads and YouTube. They believe that their albums are global components that should be heard as a whole, and any fragmentation or partial listening out of context destroys the integrity of their work. "Ellos entienden que sus discos son parte de un componente global, que debe escucharse como parte de un todo, y cualquier cosa que ayude a fragmentar eso y escuchar un trozo fuera de contexto les parece realmente cargarse su obra."

srcs.episode: Artistas que no están en Spotify y por qué

podcast.title: Protection of Artistic Integrity
podcast.body: The band actively pursues its rights on YouTube, not primarily for royalty concerns, but to prevent individual song fragments from being heard outside the context of the full album. Their singer has stated that vinyl is the perfect format, requiring listeners to engage with half an hour of music at a time, preventing arbitrary skipping. "Su cantante de hecho en varias entrevistas ha dicho que para él la música perfecta es en minilo, porque tienes que tragar medio ahora primero, medio ahora después y que no puedes coger tu un trozo y escuchar los suelto."

xref.title: Fish Farmer
xref.body: Ian Anderson, the leading man of Jethro Tull, diversified his career by becoming a fish farmer. He specifically raises salmon in the Scottish Islands, though he continues to make music as well. "Jethro Tulls, leading man Ian Anderson, became a fish farmer. He raises salmon in the Scottish Islands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Pioneering Self-Songwriting and Touring
xref.body: The band distinguished itself by writing all of its own songs, a rare feat for female artists of their time. They also toured with major acts such as Jethro Tull and Humble Pie, and their work influenced a generation of aspiring female rockers. "They released five major label albums, and they wrote all their own songs, which is something almost no female artists did back in those days."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Touring and Influence
xref.body: Fanny toured with prominent acts such as Jethro Tull and Humble Pie, and their work was instrumental in influencing a generation of aspiring female rock musicians. "They toured with big acts like Jethro Tull and Humble Pie and they influenced a generation of wannabe female rockers."
